description: We are a studio based on Cartago, Costa Rica that has worked on multiple design projects. Our team prioritize function without leaving aside the esthetics of the project. MNIOS has vast experience working on data visualization and synthetize information.
summary: We decided to take on the astronaut health challenge by creating a software that unifies all health data that is usually collected before, during ,and after the mission. An astronaut should be able to use the software to have independence for long term and far away missions where communication becomes difficult. A focus on daily check-ins for mental health with short exercises and an automatic/manual emergency system helps reduce stress and isolation in space.
details:
Our software provides a place where both astronauts and healthcare professionals can obtain statistics and predictions on cardiovascular, musculoskeletal, neurological, immune system, and biochemical health. There are also sections for sleep, physical fitness , and mental health tracking and logs.

Our two main focuses were to create a daily check-in and an automatic emergency system. To create motivation for the check-ins we created a streak system where stars are gained by checking the health hub and completing the daily questions. At the end of the daily questions there is a small activity to promote mindfulness and a stress free break. The activities change day to day based on the answers from the questions and only take a couple of minutes to complete (writing or breathing excersice, etc).

The emergency mode automatically detects, through the collected data, when a crew member is having a medical emergency. There is also a mode where an astronaut can alert other crew members they are having an emergency. The system asks basic questions and using super intelligence creates an immediate diagnostic along with a step by step on how to address the emergency. There is also a practice drill mode where a random emergency is selected from the rotation to create readiness for any situation.

We hope that having a single hub that encompasses and organizes all available medical information helps astronauts during their missions and post-mission
